### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area

body:
PR Summary by Qodo

Automate specification publishing to GitHub Wiki ✨ Enhancement 📝 Documentation ⚙️ Configuration changes 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Compile bilingual specifications into a flat, navigable GitHub Wiki structure.
>• Synchronize generated pages after specification changes or manual workflow dispatch.
>• Add the diagnostics reference to the specification index.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD A["Push or dispatch"] --> B["Sync workflow"] --> C["Wiki compiler"] --> D["Generated pages"] --> E["GitHub Wiki"] F["Specification files"] --> C ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Derive pages from one manifest
- ➕ Eliminates duplication between filenames, rewritten links, and sidebar entries - ➕ Reduces maintenance when chapters or languages are added - ➖ Requires additional generation logic for display labels and ordering - ➖ May obscure intentional Wiki page naming conventions
2. Publish with GitHub Pages
- ➕ Preserves directory structure and relative links - ➕ Supports richer static-site navigation and validation tooling - ➖ Does not satisfy the explicit GitHub Wiki publishing goal - ➖ Requires separate hosting configuration and potentially a site generator
>**Recommendation:** The dedicated Wiki compilation and push workflow is appropriate because it keeps spec/ authoritative while targeting GitHub Wiki's flat page model. Retain this architecture, but consider consolidating page metadata into one manifest if the documentation set grows, avoiding drift across FILE_MAP, link replacements, and sidebar entries.
Files changed (4) +212 / -0

Enhancement (1) +154 / -0
prepare_wiki.pyCompile specifications into Wiki-compatible pages +154/-0
>Compile specifications into Wiki-compatible pages > >
>• Adds a Python compiler that creates Home, sidebar, footer, and bilingual chapter pages in wiki_dist. It flattens source filenames and rewrites repository-relative document links to GitHub Wiki page links.
>
> >.github/scripts/prepare_wiki.py
Documentation (1) +1 / -0
README.mdIndex the diagnostics reference chapter +1/-0
>Index the diagnostics reference chapter > >
>• Adds Chapter 07 to the bilingual specification table of contents with links to the English and Japanese diagnostics references.
>
> >spec/README.md
Other (2) +57 / -0
wiki-sync.ymlBuild and publish specifications to GitHub Wiki +56/-0
>Build and publish specifications to GitHub Wiki > >
>• Adds a GitHub Actions workflow triggered by relevant main-branch changes or manual dispatch. The job generates Wiki content, clones the Wiki repository, commits changed pages, and pushes them with the GitHub Actions token.
>
> >.github/workflows/wiki-sync.yml
.gitignoreIgnore generated Wiki output +1/-0
>Ignore generated Wiki output > >
>• Excludes the temporary wiki_dist directory produced by the Wiki preparation script.
>
> >.gitignore
